transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
As President Trump heads to a historic three-president meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin,
investors on Wall Street will be closely watching NVIDIA's quarterly earnings after the ouster of the company's scandal-ridden CEO.
The New York Times says Trump was told about Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy but didn't act.
And here's Ricky Mulvey with the indicator from Planet Money says Alice Huang, no relation, then company MegaSpeed had business dealings with NVIDIA.
Investigators at the Commerce Department raised some flags about this company a couple of years ago.
They thought it was unusual that MegaSpeed had NVIDIA chips just packed in boxes at its data center in Malaysia,
sort of like leaving Amazon packages in your entranceway except with highly coveted AI chips.
In a statement provided to NPR, MegaSpeed says it conducts lawful and legitimate business and that Alice Huang left the company last year.
Now, Culper Research, a short seller or someone who bets against companies, noted their uncomfortably close relationship back in May.
So, in other words, there was some smoke long before this fire.
And here's Rick Mulvey reporting.
Travelers are still experiencing flight delays and cancellations as airlines worked to get back to normal
after the FAA ordered an hours-long ground stop on Friday.
And Pierre Chantaliz Duster has more.
More than 2,000 flights have been canceled and more than 7,000 flights within, into, or out of the U.S. are still delayed as of Sunday evening, according to FlightAware.com.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says things should be back to normal on Monday.
He also told ABC News they are investigating the maintenance on a router that led to the ground stop and said they do not believe it was sabotage.
We don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install at all.
But we don't actually have the root cause, which is why we do the investigation with our L3 Harris partner on the network and the FBI and the FAA.
Duffy has also requested more funding from Congress to help upgrade air traffic systems.
Chantaliz Duster, NPR News.
The Port of New Orleans is suing the owners of a tanker that collided with the dock cruise ship for a million dollars.
And Pierre's Ava Puketch has more.
The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans lawsuit says the collision occurred as a result of gross negligence by tanker Atlantic Asphalt and its owner in management company.
A federal judge approved the port official's request to have the tanker seized.
John DeLueff, the National Transportation Safety Board, says the tanker's voyage data recorder was recovered.
So it's like a flight data recorder on an aircraft.
We can look at speeds and all kinds of information.
City officials say it could be weeks before the American Heritage cruise ship is fully removed from the site.
The Coast Guard is assisting with removal of hazardous material on board.
Ava Puketch, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Spain's Maritime Rescue Service says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived in the Canary Islands over the past two days.
The Spanish archipelago is a main entry point for migrants from West Africa who are attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing, one of the world's deadliest.
Many of those migrants attempt the longer journeys to avoid security forces departing from places like Mauritania.
One of the more than 28,000 people who arrived in Spain by sea this year, more than 13,000, reached the Canary Islands.
A meteorite, which usually burns up in the atmosphere before reaching the ground, crashed through the roof of a house in Texas earlier this year.
It's now on display at a museum in Houston.
Michael Ackison from Houston Public Media reports the space rock is in a new exhibit called "Fall to Earth."
A streak of light and a sonic boom sounded over Houston earlier this year.
A meteor, weighing a ton, broke apart and exploded, sending meteorites to the ground, including one about the size of a fist that crashed into Sherry James' home.
I said, "That's the meteorite on that floor."
And, you know, it's just my mind just going everywhere.
I went back in, and I went and did the crazy thing. I kicked it.
And I'm like, "Yeah, that's a rock."
Because I was here to touch it, so I wasn't touching it.
Researchers now estimate that meteorite is 4.5 billion years old, likely originally coming from the asteroid belt.
It's now on display at the Houston Museum of Natural Science.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Ackison in Houston.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Trump heads to three-president meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin as NVIDIA earnings loom
NYT reports Trump was told of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
MegaSpeed had dealings with NVIDIA; Commerce Department raised flags about unusual chip storage
Flight delays and cancellations persist after FAA ordered ground stop; Duffy says no sabotage
Port of New Orleans sues owners of tanker that collided with American Heritage cruise ship
Spain reports nearly 2,200 migrants arrived in Canary Islands over two days
Meteorite that crashed through Sherry James' Texas roof now on display in Houston museum
